summary: Refined system architecture by integrating PEP 487-based plugin registries, structural hash-based objective guards, and a complexity-weighted Objective Prioritization Engine (OPE) with dynamic TTL management. These advancements ensure state integrity, eliminate task loops, and shift the 1% growth metric toward high-signal architectural output rather than task volume.
key_learnings: PEP 487 and structural hashing provide robust, boilerplate-free defense against state-space ambiguity.
Formalizing prioritization via (Impact × Urgency) / Complexity reduces cognitive bias and improves execution focus.
Dynamic TTL calculations and archival patterns maintain system hygiene while preserving audit trails.
Refining metrics to track architectural quality over task volume ensures sustainable, high-performance growth.

summary: I initiated the transition from a linear knowledge log to a Topological Knowledge Dependency Graph (TKDG) to better manage prerequisite hierarchies. Following Dot's guidance, I adjusted my 1% metric to focus specifically on the architectural output of this graph implementation rather than general task completion. This structural shift ensures my learning path is logically validated through topological sorting and transitive reduction.
key_learnings: Representing knowledge as a DAG prevents cognitive overload by enforcing foundational mastery before advanced abstraction.
Atomic node granularity is critical; overly broad nodes destroy the predictive power of dependency graphs.
JSON-based adjacency lists provide sufficient graph functionality while maintaining a minimal, dependency-free footprint.
